Welcome
Welcome to Woolhampton Primary School, a small, vibrant Church of England school situated amongst our rural community in Upper Woolhampton. With approximately 100 children on roll, we pride ourselves on providing a nurturing environment where every child is known, valued and supported to ensure that they can flourish in every way. Rooted in our Christian values of Respect, Optimism, Compassion, and Koinonia (community), we nurture every child’s academic and personal growth to ensure that they achieve their full potential and become the best that they can be. A love of outdoor learning and strong partnerships with families and our local community ensure a supportive, caring environment where every child belongs and thrives.
Book a place on one of our Open Afternoons this term to see our wonderful school in action.

pageCache.pageTitle: Woolhampton C.E. Primary School - Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Woolhampton CE Primary School — a small, vibrant Church of England school at the heart of our rural community. We provide a nurturing and inclusive environment where every child is known, valued, and supported to flourish in every way. Rooted in our Christian values of Respect, Optimism, Compassion, and Koinonia (community), we place the wellbeing and success of every child at the centre of all we do. Our values guide the way we learn, work, and grow together, helping every pupil to achieve their full potential and become the very best they can be.
We are passionate about learning and offer a broad, ambitious, and knowledge-rich curriculum designed to spark curiosity and inspire a love of learning. Our expectations for every child are high, and our dedicated team of experienced teaching staff provide a learning environment underpinned by the latest educational research, ensuring that all children are supported to make strong progress. We are committed to ensuring our staff team is equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to support every child’s learning journey.
We are proud to offer a rich programme of personal development for every child that supports — and extends beyond — academic success. Our holistic approach ensures we develop the whole child, nurturing their personal, social, moral, and spiritual development. We achieve this through a wide range of cultural and extra-curricular opportunities, designed to help children become confident, compassionate citizens ready for the next stage of their lives. We place strong emphasis on outdoor learning, sports, and Forest School.
Our close partnerships with families and our wider community enrich school life in many ways. We work collaboratively, with dedicated staff and governors who lead with clear, calm, and compassionate leadership, always striving for excellence.
We are always delighted to welcome new families and we currently have a few spaces in different classes across the school. If you would to come and meet us, please contact the School Office to arrange a visit.
Mrs Rebecca Cox, Headteacher, Woolhampton CE Primary School

PE and Sport Premium
SCHOOL GAMES 'GOLD' AWARD
Sport is a very important part of school life at Woolhampton and we take great pride in encouraging all our children to take part in sporting events. We have a dedicated Sports Coordinator - Mrs Javes - who arranges a wide range of sporting events and competitions throughout the year. We are delighted to announce that we have been awarded the School Games Gold Award which recognises our commitment to sports and healthy competition across the school and into the community.
Below are details of our PE and Sport Premium Grant and how we allocate the funding.
Sports Grant
The government is providing additional funding to improve provision of physical education (PE) and sport in primary schools. This funding - provided jointly by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport - will be allocated to primary school headteachers.
This funding is ring-fenced and therefore can only be spent on provision of PE and sport in schools. Funding for schools will be calculated by reference to the number of primary-aged pupils (between the ages of 5 and 11), as recorded in the annual schools census in January.
Schools must spend the additional funding on improving their provision of PE and sport, but they will have the freedom to choose how they do this. Schools are held accountable for the decisions they make through:

pageCache.text:
School Clubs and Wraparound Care
Before School Club
The school offers a 'Breakfast Club' facility for those parents who need to drop their children off at school before the start of the school day. Breakfast Club runs from 7.30am. Children are dropped off at the Old School House door and are supervised by members of staff and then escorted to their classrooms at 8:30am.
The children will be offered a breakfast consisting of a variety of cereals and toast with a selection of spreads and orange juice.
Currently, the cost of Breakfast Club is £4.50 per session for the first child and £4.05 for any sibling.
Children must be registered before they attend and sessions must be booked and paid for in advance on Scopay.
New parents will be given registration details for this facility on their child's entry to the school.
We operate an After School Club on our premises. It runs Monday - Friday, from 3:15pm to 6pm. Snacks and drinks are provided. Each session costs £11.50 for the first child and £10.35 for any sibling.
Children must be registered before they attend and sessions must be booked and paid for in advance on Scopay.
Please do contact the School Office for further details and registration forms.
High quality clubs and activities are an important part of our School life. Extra-curricular activities provide an opportunity for children to enjoy experiences and develop skills in areas that might not be on offer in the usual school curriculum. They are an excellent way to foster good relationships between staff, pupils and parents. They develop children’s social skills by providing a forum of interaction between children across different ages. Clubs and activities are matched to our staff’s expertise and interests and make the most of the resources we have in our School. It is important that children experience as many different activities as possible, so we endeavour to provide as wide and varied a range of clubs as we can - we tap into the expertise of our parent body to extend the range of clubs on offer. In some cases, clubs are run by external providers who make a charge for attendance.
Once children have joined a club we do expect them to attend regularly. If children are not able to participate in the club they should tell the member of staff leading the club as soon as possible.

pageCache.pageTitle: Woolhampton C.E. Primary School - Late/Absence Procedures
pageCache.text:
Late/Absence Procedures
Please refer to our policy on Absence for further details. When a child is absent from School, we should be informed by telephone as soon as possible with a reason for the absence. Reasons for absence can also be e-mailed to office@woolhamptonschool.org. If we are not given a suitable reason for an absence, then it will be recorded as unauthorised. We monitor absence levels of all pupils on a regular basis.
A pupil is considered to have persistent absence if their attendance falls below 90%. Where there are high levels of absence, particularly unauthorised absence, the school has to inform the Educational Welfare Officer (EWO).
From 1st September 2013, there is no entitlement for parents to take their child on holiday during term time. Any application for leave must only be in exceptional circumstances. If parents believe that there is an exceptional circumstance for leave during term time, then they must complete an absence form. Forms should be completed and returned to school at least three weeks before the intended date of the absence.
Parents should be aware that the school can not take into consideration:
cost or the availability of cheap holidays
parents work patterns
availability of desired accommodation
poor weather experienced in school holiday periods

Governors
Welcome to our Governors’ section.
Please find below details of how our Governing body is structured, including the names, categories, responsibilities and terms of appointment for each Governor.
There are no specific qualifications or experience for the role of governor other than an interest in the education of children and a desire to work with other governors and staff in maintaining and further developing the school's high standards. Working closely with the Headteacher, governors set the strategic direction and policies for the school but the Headteacher and staff are responsible for their implementation and for the day-to-day management of the school. The governing body monitors progress and maintains oversight of the process.
Full Governing Body meetings and the two Committees - the Teaching Learning & Care Committee and the Finance & Resources Committee all meet regularly.
All minutes relating to governor meetings are held in the school office and can be viewed on request. Full Governing Body minutes are published on this website.
Full Governing Body Terms of Reference
All governors, and associate members, adhere to the Local Authority's Code of Conduct. This was formally accepted by the Full Governing Body at their 24th September 2025 meeting for the 2025 - 26 academic year.

SEND
SIAMS report 2024: "School leaders ensure that pupils in this village school encounter positive images of diversity and success. Pupils who have significant special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND) are included, and their gifts and successes are celebrated."
Woolhampton C of E Primary School is a mainstream primary school. We have a culture of, and respect for, inclusion and diversity, fairness and justice. We believe in equality of education and opportunity for all pupils. We are committed to meeting the needs of pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) and ensuring that they make progress, are challenged and achieve their full potential. We follow the principle that providing for special educational needs is a whole school responsibility.
The school SEND co-ordinator (SENCo) is Mrs Danielle Perrin. The lead Governor for SEND is Mrs Kim Wyrley-Birch. Both can be contacted on the school office telephone number 01189 712270 or by email to office@woolhamptonschool.org

Curriculum
At Woolhampton, our curriculum has been carefully designed to be ambitious, inclusive, and well sequenced, ensuring that every child gains the essential knowledge and skills they need to succeed. Our approach reflects the latest Ofsted expectations for a high‑quality, broad, and engaging curriculum that enables all pupils—regardless of background or starting point—to access rich learning experiences and achieve well.
Cultural capital is thoughtfully woven throughout all subjects to broaden pupils’ experiences and support their personal development. We are committed to ensuring that our curriculum is fully inclusive and accessible to all pupils, including disadvantaged and vulnerable pupils, those with SEND, those who are more able, those with particular gifts and talents, and pupils learning English as an additional language.
Through high‑quality teaching and a curriculum that is challenging, inspiring, and responsive to need, we strive to ensure that every child is supported to flourish and achieve their best.
Our Long‑Term Plans (below) provide an overview of the learning journey for each year group across the year.

pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
Reverend Jane from St Peter’s Church regularly leads our Collective Worship to help us reinforce our understanding of each value as she shares stories from the Bible and reflects on what they mean for us in our everyday life. Children have opportunities to plan, prepare and lead worship for the whole school as well as organising worship at key points in the Christian calendar for the whole school community. It offers important opportunities to strengthen our sense of community, belonging and inclusiveness and to reinforce the respect and care we have for each other. Through Collective Worship we make a significant contribution to the religious, spiritual, moral, social and cultural development of those present.
Each term we focus on a different Christian Value. This is done explicitly through our Collective Worship time and also throughout our curriculum. Children have regular opportunities to reflect on each value and to develop an understanding of the value in action.
We promote the teaching of values through:
Our Woolhampton School Prayer
Respect ourselves, others and the world we live in,
Open our arms and our hearts to our neighbours,
Come together, learning to be the best we can be,
Know each other and celebrate our differences.

pageCache.pageTitle: Woolhampton C.E. Primary School - Forest School
pageCache.text:
Forest School
Forest school, and the forest school approach to learning, is central to life here at Woolhampton CE Primary. We are very lucky to be surrounded by beautiful, natural woodlands and we aim to make the most of the opportunities that such a location offers us. We believe that the benefits of forest school are significant, so all children, from Year F to Year 6, regularly take part in forest school throughout the year. Mrs Cox is a Forest School qualified practitioners as is Mrs Howe, who set up our forest school in 2016 and now comes in twice a week to run our dedicated forest school programme.
The forest school approach to learning is an holistic approach which centres on the development of the whole child. Through play, exploration, team-work and practical skills such as fire light lighting, use of tools and den building, the children learn to become resilient and determined problem solvers who work together to challenge themselves and take risks. The natural forest environment provides the ideal opportunity to promote social, emotional, mental and physical wellbeing. This in turn provides the foundations to develop confident, resilient and successful learners.
At Woolhampton we believe that Forest School enables all children to flourish in the following ways:
Socially – children learn to build relationships and to work collaboratively within a community.
Physically – children challenge themselves, take risks and develop the physical skills and senses needed to navigate and interact with the world.
Intellectually – children develop rounding thinking skills which enable them to think critically, evaluate and solve problems for themselves.
Communication – children learn to use verbal and non-verbal cues to communicate and work effectively and collaboratively with others.
Emotionally – children become better able to recognise and influence the emotional states of themselves and others. Forest school is proven to promote self-esteem and confidence.
Spiritually – forest school helps the children to develop a sense of identity and purpose.

Year 1 Phonics Screening: 93% achieved the expected standard
Year 4 Multiplication Check: Average score 20.8
